says: A process's view watchers are kept only in a Set in the runner's memory, so once the Process object sleeps or is evicted, later view patches go to nobody until the client opens the view again.
proof: Runner.ts:225 'const clients = new Set<string>()' is the only store of watchers; it is filled only by open at Runner.ts:1333 and read by publish at Runner.ts:868. The runner lives in the object's runtime, a class field built in the constructor (next/apps/fabrika/src/brain.ts:208). Cloudflare's lifecycle docs: an idle object with no socket is evicted after 70 to 140 s, and when hibernated 'the in-memory state is discarded'; experiment 231 saw the constructor run again after 15 s idle on workerd. The Process object holds no socket, so a client watching over the Connection object's socket keeps its socket while the Process forgets it. worker-supervision.test.ts:382 calls view.open again after an abort and never checks that a patch reaches a watcher opened before it.
cost: A window watching a program stops getting updates after the program's object is idle for a minute or two, with no error; it looks frozen.
